result.heading: Coverage provided
result.text:
Meridian Mutual will pay for direct physical loss to covered property caused by water, or
waterborne material, which:

1. **backs up through sewers or drains**; or
2. **overflows or is discharged from a sump, sump pump or related equipment**, even where
   the overflow results from mechanical breakdown of the sump pump.

Coverage applies to Coverage A, Coverage B and Coverage C property, and to Coverage D
loss of use arising from a covered water backup event.

result.heading: Claim handling note
result.text:
Water backup claims are assigned to the **Property — Water team** and carry a target
first-contact time of **one business day** from First Notice of Loss. A moisture-mapping
inspection is required before any payment above **$5,000**.

result.heading: Deductible
result.text:
A **separate deductible of $500** applies to each water backup occurrence. This deductible
applies **instead of**, not in addition to, the base all-perils deductible of $1,000.

result.heading: Conditions
result.text:
Coverage under this endorsement applies **only if**:

- the sump pump and any related equipment were in **proper working order** at the time of
  loss; and
- for dwellings with a finished basement, a **battery backup sump system or water alarm**
  is installed, where the dwelling was built or the basement finished after 01 January 2020.

Where the required backup system is absent, the limit is reduced to **$2,500** rather than
being voided entirely.

result.heading: My basement flooded after heavy rain. Am I covered?
result.text:
It depends on how the water got in. If water **backed up through a drain or sewer**, or a
**sump pump overflowed**, and you have endorsement HO-2026-01, you are covered up to
$10,000 (or $25,000 if you chose the higher limit) with a $500 deductible. If **surface
water flowed in** from outside — over the ground, through a window well, or from a river or
storm surge — that is **flood**, and flood is not covered by any endorsement in this pack.
Flood cover must be bought separately.

- natural gas and steam lines

dwelling** and ends at the utility company's connection point or the boundary of the
residence premises, whichever comes first.

result.heading: Endorsement HO-2026-08 — Roof Surfaces Actual Cash Value and Wind/Hail Schedule
result.text:
**Attaches to:** HO-3-2026 base form
**Effective:** 01 March 2026
**Premium:** credit of $145 to $410 annually depending on roof age and territory
**Endorsement pack:** 2026 Spring Release

---

result.heading: What this endorsement does
result.text:
This is a **coverage-restricting endorsement** applied in exchange for a premium credit. It
changes the loss settlement basis for **roof surfacing** from replacement cost to
**actual cash value** where the loss is caused by **windstorm or hail**.

All other causes of loss to the roof — fire, falling objects, weight of ice and snow,
vandalism, aircraft, vehicles, explosion — continue to be settled on the base form
replacement cost basis. The restriction applies **only** to wind and hail.

result.heading: When this endorsement may not be applied
My roof was damaged by hail. Why is the cheque less than the estimate?
result.text:
If endorsement HO-2026-08 is on your policy — which you would have accepted in exchange for
a premium credit — the roof surfacing is settled at **actual cash value** for wind and hail
losses. We take the replacement cost, subtract your windstorm deductible, then apply
depreciation based on the roof's age and material. A 12-year-old asphalt shingle roof
depreciates at 5% a year, so about 60% is deducted.

Damage to the **decking, ceilings and interior** is still paid at full replacement cost.
Only the outer surfacing is depreciated.

result.heading: Deductibles
result.text:
The base all-perils deductible is **$1,000 per occurrence**, applied to Section I property
losses only. No deductible applies to Coverage E or Coverage F.

A separate **windstorm or hail deductible of 2% of the Coverage A limit** applies in
designated coastal territories, as shown in the Declarations. Where both the all-perils and
the windstorm deductible could apply to a single occurrence, only the **larger** of the two
is deducted.

result.heading: Depreciation schedule
result.text:
Actual cash value is calculated as replacement cost less depreciation, applied by roof age
and material as follows:

| Roof material | Expected life | Annual depreciation | Maximum depreciation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Composition / asphalt shingle (3-tab) | 20 years | 5.0% per year | 80% |
| Architectural / laminated shingle | 30 years | 3.3% per year | 70% |
| Wood shake or shingle | 25 years | 4.0% per year | 75% |
| Metal panel or standing seam | 40 years | 2.5% per year | 60% |
| Clay or concrete tile | 50 years | 2.0% per year | 50% |
| Slate | 60 years | 1.7% per year | 50% |
| Modified bitumen / built-up flat roof | 20 years | 5.0% per year | 80% |

Roof age is measured from the **date the roof surfacing was last fully replaced**, as
evidenced by a permit, a contractor invoice, or the underwriting inspection photograph on
file. Where the roof age **cannot be established**, the age of the dwelling is used.

result.heading: Section I — Exclusions
result.text:
The following are excluded under the base form. Some may be added back by endorsement.

1. **Ordinance or law** — increased costs from enforcement of any building code.
   *May be added back by endorsement HO-2026-05.*
2. **Earth movement** — earthquake, landslide, sinkhole, mudflow, subsidence.
3. **Water damage** — flood, surface water, waves, tidal water, overflow of a body of
   water, and **water which backs up through sewers or drains**.
   *Sewer and drain backup may be added back by endorsement HO-2026-01.*
4. **Power failure** occurring off the residence premises.
5. **Neglect** of an insured to use reasonable means to save and preserve property.
6. **War**, including undeclared war and civil war.
7. **Nuclear hazard.**
8. **Intentional loss** by or at the direction of an insured.
9. **Governmental action** — seizure or destruction by order of a public authority.
10. **Wear and tear**, marring, deterioration, mechanical breakdown, latent defect,
    rust, mould, wet or dry rot, and smog.
    *Mechanical and electrical breakdown may be added back by endorsement HO-2026-03.*

---

result.heading: What this endorsement does
result.text:
Exclusion 3 of the base form excludes water which backs up through sewers or drains. This
endorsement **deletes that portion of the exclusion** and adds the coverage described
below. All other terms of exclusion 3 — including flood, surface water and overflow of a
body of water — remain fully excluded and are **not** restored by this endorsement.

result.heading: Exclusions specific to this endorsement
result.text:
Scheduled property coverage does not apply to loss caused by:

- **wear and tear**, gradual deterioration, insects or vermin
- **inherent vice** or any repairing, restoring or retouching process
- **mysterious disappearance of unscheduled items** — this remains a Coverage C theft
  question under the base form
- breakage of fragile articles such as glassware or porcelain, **unless** caused by fire,
  theft, vandalism, or the collapse of a building — this breakage exclusion does not apply
  to scientific instruments, cameras or musical instruments
- loss occurring while the property is in the custody of a **transportation carrier** for
  stamp or coin collections

result.heading: What this endorsement does
result.text:
Exclusion 10 of the base form excludes mechanical breakdown, latent defect and damage
from artificially generated electrical current. This endorsement **adds back** coverage for
sudden and accidental **breakdown of covered equipment** at the residence premises.

result.heading: What this endorsement does
result.text:
Exclusion 1 of the base form excludes the increased cost of construction that results from
enforcement of a building code, ordinance or law. This endorsement **increases the
ordinance or law allowance** to the percentage of the Coverage A limit shown in the
Declarations.

Without this endorsement, the base form provides an ordinance or law allowance of
**10% of the Coverage A limit**. With this endorsement, the allowance is increased to
either **25%** or **50%** of the Coverage A limit, as elected.
